understandability.claim: README documents the Minecraft/NeoForge target, build and installation paths, server behavior, configuration, client scanner, privacy and enforcement limits, data-pack extension points, administrator commands, persistence, evidence logs, and security limitations.

verification.claim: The stable candidate records one exact-head gate spanning Build, GameTest, Packaged Server, External Runtime, and Ubuntu/Windows/macOS scanner checks; all required workflows succeeded and all 24 required GameTests passed.

A packaged NeoForge server and real Minecraft protocol client exercised a real block-break packet through BlockEvent.BreakEvent, production warning progression, JSONL evidence logging, and actual connection termination with action=kick.

reproducibility.claim: The build records Java 21, Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.235, mod version 1.1.0, test dependencies, production/gameTest source separation, and the Gradle build path.

An isolated offline clean build succeeded and produced a JAR byte-for-byte identical to the GitHub-built stable candidate with SHA-256 4cc843c0c39348203e3ffe30ab4dbd6c33a9eb0f6d2907913d005b89a80588fe.

interoperability.claim: The repository defines exact Minecraft/NeoForge compatibility, separate server-only and optional client installation modes, behavior with FakePlayers and tools from other mods, and data-pack tags that other content can extend.

Scanner and recursive filesystem-watcher behavior passed on Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS; this evidence is bounded to scanner/watcher behavior and does not claim a complete graphical Minecraft runtime on all three platforms.

security-safety.claim: The client scanner explicitly documents fail-open/fail-closed policy, high-confidence blocking boundaries, privacy behavior, non-attestation, false-positive limits, and that it is not a tamper-proof or server-enforced anti-cheat.

stewardship.claim: Repository build metadata records MIT licensing and stable version 1.1.0.
The release receipt freezes exact artifact identity and requires publication from the reviewed stable-candidate JAR without rebuilding it after approval.

claimBoundaries: Only the default public-claim-context revision 8caaab65266a94e7bdedc6ad2f66030c7e394edf is assessed.
Open NeoForge port PR #1 and stacked dependency-range PR #2 are unmerged and excluded from this repository-snapshot Quality evidence.
GameTest run configuration is build configuration only; no default-branch GameTest source or exact-head runtime receipt is treated as verification evidence.

understandability.claim: README documents the public-claim ownership model, player and manager permissions, client/server installation requirement, commands, anti-grief defaults, claim limits, supported Minecraft/Forge/FTB versions, and the internal FTB Teams compatibility boundary.

reproducibility.claim: The default snapshot records Java 17, Minecraft 1.20.1, Forge 47.4.13, official 1.20.1 mappings, exact FTB Chunks 2001.3.6, FTB Teams 2001.3.1, FTB Library 2001.2.12, Architectury 9.1.12, and the Gradle build path.

maintainability.claim: The repository identifies private/internal FTB Teams 2001.3.1 behavior as a version-specific compatibility risk and isolates that dependency in a dedicated FTBServerTeamBridge instead of scattering it through the public-claim service and packet layers.

interoperability.claim: The snapshot declares exact FTB component versions, both-side dependency requirements, the Forge/Minecraft compatibility range, and the client UI plus custom networking requirement; README separately documents why the private FTB Teams boundary is pinned.

security-safety.claim: Public-claim mutations are bounded server-side by enable/manager checks, per-project capacity, player distance, adjacency, existing-claim protection, a 64-change packet limit, and rejection of malformed packet counts; default team policy also disables explosions, mob griefing, PVP, and fake-player block editing.

stewardship.claim: The default snapshot carries an MIT license, explicit project identity/version metadata, and repository-local engineering guidance that preserves ownership/capacity isolation, exact compatibility evidence, persistence/client-server boundaries, and the distinction between default history and active unmerged port carriers.
